chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Salih ibn Sahl who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the believers from the clay of the Prophets?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاء: The Prophets — specifically the chain of divinely sent messengers
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُون: The believers — those of true faith (iman), especially the devoted followers of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.طِينَة: Clay, primordial essence — the substance from which humans were created; in Shia hadith literature, denotes the metaphysical origin/nature of the soul

ai.seo_question: Are believers created from the same clay as the Prophets in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Salih ibn Sahl asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether believers share in the primordial clay (tina) from which the Prophets were created, and the Imam affirms this with a simple 'yes.' This hadith belongs to the theological teaching in al-Kafi concerning the metaphysical origin of believers, positing that true believers are ontologically linked to the Prophets through a shared noble substance. In Shia cosmological thought, 'clay' (tina) refers to the primordial substance or essence from which souls are fashioned, not physical earth alone, indicating that believers possess an inherent spiritual affinity with the Prophets.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Salih Bin Sahl who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The Momineen (plural of Momin) are from the clay of the Prophetsas?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Salih ibn Sahl who has said the following:
“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Are the believers made from the clay from which the prophets were made?’ He said, ‘Yes, that is correct.’”
